title: ConflictResolved
description:
Payload of `notes.conflict.resolved.v1` (contract `notes/conflict.v1`): the channel
acknowledged the `resolve_conflict` write that names this conflict, and the conflict is closed.

A fact. The enclosing envelope carries the owner as `tenant_id` (`user:<id>`) and the
aggregate `notes_conflict:<conflict_id>`. The payload carries the resulting revision hash and
never file content. Every member it does not declare is refused.

connection_id.description: The connection whose vault holds the file.

operation_id.description: The Platform operation of kind `notes.file.write` of the `resolve_conflict` write.

origin.description: Who asked for the resolution: `platform` or `site:<site id>`.

path.description: The path of the file, relative to the vault root, in NFC.

revision.description:
The lowercase hex SHA-256 of the revision that is current after the resolution. For
`keep_current` it is the revision that was current when the conflict was raised.

VaultPath.title: VaultPath
VaultPath.description:
A file path relative to the vault root, segments separated by `/`.

Not empty, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, no leading or trailing `/`, no empty, `.` or `..`
segment, no backslash and no C0 or DEL control character, so a path can never name a file
outside the vault.

The path is in Unicode NFC. This contract does not check NFC: the producer normalises
every path before it publishes one, and a consumer may rely on it.

WriteOrigin.title: WriteOrigin
WriteOrigin.description:
Who asked for a write: `platform` for the Ratatoskr API, or `site:<site id>` for a site in
owner mode.

A site id has 3 to 40 lower-case ASCII letters, digits and `-`. Every other value is
refused. `ratatoskr-notes` records the origin with the write and repeats it in a conflict
that the write raises.
